column2: Act Two
None of Our Young Classmates Are Losers
Every Junior Has A Good Time

The secretly circulated History of Shilan: Legends records that Lu Mingfei spent six years at school awkward, timid, and good for nothing. According to his cousin Lu Mingze, the legendary Lu had a pitiful background: his parents had abandoned him, gone abroad, and failed to show their faces for seven or eight years. Fostered at his uncle's house, he ate an enormous amount, a complete glutton... At Shilan High School, where outstanding people gathered, someone like him was a roadside weed, stepped on deliberately or otherwise by everyone.
At Sophie Lad Pizza, Lu Mingfei sat alone in a private room... carrying a toilet seat.
Damn it! Was this how you showed up to a Literature Club lunch? He looked like a foreign monk from the Western Regions arriving to wreck the place with some exotic weapon!

He had originally been in high spirits, but a courteous waiter stopped him at the door and knocked him senseless with one blow: “Out! Our restrooms all have squat toilets. We don't buy your toilet seats.”

Lu Mingfei knew it looked bad, but what could he do? His aunt's orders outranked heaven. Even his uncle had to kneel on a keyboard if he disobeyed; who was Lu Mingfei to defy the decree? The building-supply market was some distance from his uncle's house, and after calculating every way, he had realized that buying the seat would leave no time to go home before lunch. He had to come straight here. Even then he had jogged all the way with the seat around his neck, feeling as if he wore the breastplate of a sacred suit of armor... and still he was the only one on time.
“Can't these people be more reliable?” The thought made him increasingly angry.

Apart from that, he was nervous. He hadn't seen a certain person in a long time and didn't know what expression to wear. People young and ignorant about love usually showed two symptoms: picking the least unfortunate-looking girl in class as their dream lover and even contemplating marrying her; and believing they could act convincingly before her, trying to produce a smile that would dazzle her without considering that nature had given them a bitter-melon face poorly suited to smiling.
Fortunately Lu Mingfei did not have a bitter-melon face. If he had to be compared to a vegetable, he was more like celery left too long in the sun...
The door opened, and in came someone short and plump, with a round belly no belt could contain.
“What's with that? Carrying a toilet?” The newcomer was startled by Lu Mingfei's appearance.
“Xu Yanyan?” He recognized him.

He was one of the twins in their class. At the Literature Club farewell, Zhao Menghua had declared his love to Chen Wenwen with an illuminated I love you display. Lu Mingfei had played the lowercase i; the Xu brothers had played the o. After a year apart they looked more like o's than ever.
Xu Yanyan looked him up and down. “Are you... all right?”
“I'm fine.” Lu Mingfei was a little wooden, still rehearsing his long-awaited reunion smile in his head.
Nervous, Xu Yanyan perched on the edge of a chair and watched him from the corner of his eye.
Lu Mingfei was a legend at Shilan High.

As the city's foremost elite school, Shilan had no shortage of legends. Grade-ten pianists, grade-eight pipa players, and students who had passed College English Test Band Six were as plentiful as fish crossing a river. Each graduating class sent four or five scholarship students to America or Europe, and the school had supplied athletes to the national swim team and produced nationally ranked martial artists. One such fellow looked like a wandering hero, specialized in twin sabers, cut a dashing figure, and came from a wealthy family that chauffeured him in a Lexus. Whenever people saw him seated bolt upright in the rear of a luxury sedan, legs planted as though in a horse stance, two practice blades on his back and red tassels streaming over his shoulders... it was hard not to become a legend.
But once Lu Mingfei rose at Shilan High, every other legend paled.

The secretly circulated History of Shilan: Legends records that Lu Mingfei spent six years at school awkward, timid, and good for nothing. According to his cousin Lu Mingze, the legendary Lu had a pitiful background: his parents had abandoned him, gone abroad, and failed to show their faces for seven or eight years. Fostered at his uncle's house, he ate an enormous amount, a complete glutton... Naturally his grades were miserable, and he had a loose tongue; you never knew what nonsense would come out next. In class he either smiled dreamily out the window or sneaked naps in the back row, drooling all over his desk. No one attended parent-teacher meetings for him; presumably even his uncle and aunt couldn't bear the embarrassment.
At Shilan High, where outstanding people gathered, someone like him was a roadside weed, stepped on deliberately or otherwise by everyone.

His only talent was StarCraft. He made it work, mooching countless hours of internet access and drinks at cafés under the pretext of “teaching matches.” Anyone wanting a few pointers only had to say, “Lu Mingfei, let's go to the internet café after school. I'll pay for your time and buy you a Nutritional Express drink,” and he would sidle right up, shameless and ingratiating, without a shred of a teacher's dignity.
But legends are often made by a sudden, mysterious rise, blazing across the sky like a meteor!

Before his graduation, at the Literature Club farewell, everyone cheered when golden boy Zhao Menghua and beauty-ranked Chen Wenwen finally confessed and joined hands, while laughing at the legendary Lu for having once entertained improper hopes about someone...
An angel descended, bearing a sword!

A breathtaking young woman in the legendary Lu's service pushed open the doors, her beauty outshining the moon, bringing a whole company of pretty girls and an assortment of handsome clothes for him. She was all demure obedience before Lu Mingfei, and finally took his arm and whisked him away in a Ferrari.

Everyone talked about her beauty and presence: alluring and fierce, flowers and swords flying together. Shilan's boys were astonished and jealous; the girls felt that even all of them together could not match the grace of a single glance from her!

After that, Lu Mingfei shed his loser destiny and his life changed utterly. Soon news came that he had received the largest scholarship in Shilan's history to attend Cassell College, a private elite American university. Its admissions were so strict that all Shilan's top students had been rejected at interview, yet it seemed to beg Lu Mingfei to enroll. Later its principal sent Shilan's principal an enthusiastic letter thanking him for educating such a fine student. Comparing the letter's lavish praise with Lu Mingfei's transcript, which had crawled and struggled along the passing line, the principal felt his entire life had been an illusion.
Xu Yanyan secretly examined Lu Mingfei. After a year apart the legendary figure dressed just as before: a big white T-shirt, baggy shorts, and a pair of very unconvincing imitation Nikes.
As hopelessly uncool as ever.

Xu Yanyan decided to be cautious. With his stunning girl, Ferrari, and immense scholarship, Lu Mingfei had shattered countless people's confidence and risen to number one on Shilan's “This Villain Must Be Eliminated” list, an enemy every boy was entitled to kill. People could not bear seeing someone once beneath them rise to a height they had to look up at. But Xu Yanyan couldn't read him and dared not leap out and strike at once to rid the boys of this menace...

Xu Yanyan and Lu Mingfei had actually gotten along reasonably well before, but when someone in the group chat said Lu Mingfei was coming today, Xu's heart still skipped. Lu had been someone nobody respected, and Xu Yanyan had treated him coldly a few times. Now Lu Mingfei was a big shot, looking lost in another world and too indifferent to pay him attention. Who knew whether he held a grudge?

Lu Mingfei had not noticed Xu Yanyan watching. He was practicing his smile again, the corners of his mouth twitching stiffly. To Xu Yanyan it was a smile overflowing with indescribable murderous intent.
“Are you... fixing a toilet?” Xu Yanyan asked cautiously.
“No... I brought my own seat. It's more comfortable.” Lu Mingfei didn't understand the question, but nonsense came naturally to his lips.
“Good for you.” Xu Yanyan felt even less certain. A man with tens of thousands a year in scholarship money, a wealthy young master fixing toilets? Successful yet humble: a formidable rival indeed!
Another person entered, looking as though cast from the same mold as Xu Yanyan. He glanced at Lu Mingfei and also started. “Lu Mingfei? Are you... all right?”
“I'm fine, I'm fine.” Lu Mingfei didn't understand why everyone asked.

The private room fell strangely quiet. Brothers Xu Yanyan and Xu Miaomiao spoke in low voices, stealing occasional glances at the legend opposite them. His gaze was vacant, he smiled from time to time, and he held a toilet seat. Though they couldn't read him, his murderous aura was unmistakable.

Fifteen minutes later people arrived in twos and threes. Every time the door opened a familiar face appeared, startled into asking if Lu Mingfei was all right, until he began to feel a little crazy himself and scratched his head with an embarrassed smile. Finally even Liu Miaomiao, the pretty pianist who rarely took part in Literature Club activities, arrived. The gathering had become a small class reunion. The room grew lively as everyone exchanged news, and fewer people paid attention to Lu Mingfei.
“What's on special?” Xu Yanyan studied the menu.
“Who cares? Zhao Menghua said he's paying for everything today. A fully loaded surf-and-turf pizza each and unlimited cola refills!” Xu Miaomiao announced.
“Country bumpkin! If Young Master Zhao's paying, why pizza? I'll have black-truffle meat-sauce pasta with Caspian caviar!” someone said.
“Keep pretending! Caspian caviar? Do you even know where the Caspian is?” Xu Miaomiao jeered. “That stuff won't fill you up. What's the point?”
“I saw it was the most expensive... I'm sharpening my knife to fleece Zhao Menghua. Haven't you heard? His family's company is going public. It'd be a waste not to!”
“Young Master Zhao's more of a class enemy every day! He's about to overtake...” Xu Miaomiao glanced at Lu Mingfei. “...and become number one on the 'This Villain Must Be Eliminated' list!”
“The boss has always been the class enemy among class enemies,” one of Zhao Menghua's followers chimed in.

Only Liu Miaomiao was quiet, sitting obediently with her hands on her knees and smiling with pursed lips. She had always been a pretty girl who spoke softly and seemed a little delicate, looking a year or two younger than the others, with long fair hands, grade-ten piano skills, and sweet, well-behaved eyes. The boys in Lu Mingfei's class had split into three camps: one supporting the “Little Celestial Princess” Su Xiaoqiang, another declaring Liu Miaomiao much prettier than Su, and the rest under Chen Wenwen's banner.
Lu Mingfei let his thoughts wander through his school days. Chen Wenwen had still not arrived.
“You're at Fudan?” he tried, making conversation with Liu Miaomiao.

He had once been a stalwart champion in Chen Wenwen's camp, dismissing Liu Miaomiao as a little kid. In truth he admitted to himself that she was pretty, but he couldn't stand seeing boys flock around her like male attendants to a little goddess. He had even heard two of her admirers confide in each other: “I guess I won't get to marry Liu Miaomiao in this life. I'll let you have her!” The other had thumped his chest and said, “Don't worry. I'll treat her well!”
What kind of brotherly loyalty was that?

But Liu Miaomiao had been nice enough to Lu Mingfei, willing to talk to him. Once, bored, he asked how she practiced piano. She said it was hard work and you had to train finger strength from childhood. Then she played several measures powerfully with one hand against the window, making the glass tremble. Lu Mingfei couldn't produce that effect. He remembered the beautiful patterns of light and shadow her long, slender fingers left on the glass, and never called her a little kid again.
“Mm.” Liu Miaomiao nodded.

She wore a Dai-style tube skirt dyed with blue silk-tree blossoms and a white camisole, her hair in a high ponytail. She even had light makeup on. In less than a year the little kid had blossomed; sleazy middle-aged men would probably turn to look if she walked down the street now. A year had passed and everyone seemed to have changed a little. None of their young classmates were losers.

Lu Mingfei glanced at the mirror. The fellow in it looked unlucky, his messy head like a clump of chicken feathers. He wanted to cover his face. Who would have thought Cassell's elite education could produce something like this? He had once read in Zhiyin that whether a person could become an aristocrat depended on their surroundings before age thirteen. Sure enough, a bumpkin was a bumpkin for life. Even if he drove his Bugatti Veyron here, he wouldn't have Caesar's aura of a crown prince arriving.
Head drooping, he stood to escape the noisy room and wander outside. He pushed the door open. Bang.
Outside was an enormous face with a red mark down the middle, struck by the edge of the glass door.

Zhao Menghua, today's host and benefactor, stared at him as though he'd seen a ghost, unable to understand how Lu Mingfei could remain so calm after hitting him. In the past Zhao had paid for drinks and internet access while Lu flattered him; they had worked together beautifully. Now Lu Mingfei's eyes were vacant, as though he saw no one or his mind was far away.
“I'm fine, I'm fine,” Lu Mingfei said hastily, coming to himself. Habit had taken over: those had been his first words to every classmate today.
“I... I'm not!” Zhao Menghua clutched his head.
In the past Zhao would have exploded, but for the moment he didn't dare. He couldn't read Lu Mingfei.

Zhao Menghua had been the city's top scorer in their year's college entrance exams and entered Peking University's Guanghua School of Management. His family had connections, and a place as a Yale exchange student in his junior or senior year was already arranged. Everything was wonderful; he should have been a legend himself. But their year had produced Lu Mingfei, a dark horse as black as a lump of coal, who stole all his glory. Shilan's old principal had no idea what Cassell College was, but when he calculated Lu Mingfei's scholarship at roughly 300,000 yuan a year, he was astounded. When the entrance-exam results were posted, Lu Mingfei's name appeared above top scorer Zhao Menghua, on a line of its own, truly outshining everyone! Zhao gazed up at the huge red notice while the crowd discussed the legendary Lu Mingfei. Him? That lowercase i? Zhao was so depressed he nearly spat blood.
Lu Mingfei went out, Zhao Menghua came in, and the door closed between them. Inside, a chorus called, “Boss!”

In the long corridor, fierce sunlight came from the right, erasing darkness layer by layer. Long shadows of windows and a person lay across the floor. The figure's long hair and skirt hem shifted gently in the breeze. Lu Mingfei slowly turned his head right and saw a white cotton dress and a book held in hands folded over it.
The corridor was long, but unfortunately it was empty. Nothing could obstruct their view of each other.
Silence.
“It's not like I'm meeting my first girlfriend. Why am I such a coward?” All the smiles he had prepared came to nothing. Seeing her again, he still didn't know what expression to wear.
“Chen Wenwen: Lu Mingfei's first unrequited crush, three years long, ended without result; she fell to Zhao Menghua.”

If Lu Mingfei had a life file and reread it in old age, that would be all it said about Chen Wenwen. They had never held hands, seen a movie, or traveled together; he had never had the slightest chance. An unremarkable unrequited love. In the gradually fading memories, what sometimes flashed past was the hem of a white dress on a bench on the first day of school and the light and shadow across the girl's face.
“Hi, Lu Mingfei,” Chen Wenwen said.
“Oh, I'm going to the restroom,” he said.
They passed each other.

Lu Mingfei wandered around the restroom and returned to find the pizza already served, everyone eating with enthusiasm. The splendid toilet seat lay on his chair, with Chen Wenwen seated beside it. He hesitated, but that was the only seat left. He sat down gingerly and forked a piece of pizza onto his plate. Chen Wenwen smiled and nodded; perhaps she hadn't slept well, for her complexion was poor. After two bites he looked up and realized Zhao Menghua sat opposite them.
“What the hell?” he muttered inwardly.
Chen Wenwen was Zhao Menghua's girlfriend. Naturally she should sit with him.

He worried they were playing another trick on him; it wouldn't be the first. Looking around, he suddenly realized they were seated this way because of him. No one had chosen the seat beside Lu Mingfei, and Chen Wenwen had arrived last, leaving her only that place.
“Should I swap seats with someone?” he asked Chen Wenwen awkwardly.

Chen Wenwen shook her head, busy texting. When she finished she placed her phone face down on the table and began drinking cream-of-mushroom soup. The bowl hid her face; Lu Mingfei couldn't even steal a glance.
Across the room Zhao Menghua's phone beeped. He read the new message, sent a brief reply, and also laid his phone face down.
“Boss, you've really made it!” A follower reached for Zhao's hand.
“Only just noticed?” Zhao shook it, a little uncomfortable. “Why are you shaking my hand? What's this about?”
“Who wants to hold a man's hand? I wanted to see your watch.” The follower seized his wrist, revealing a heavy watch whose face shimmered faintly gold and blue. “Rolex?”
“Wow, a Yacht-Master! Caliber 4016! Boss, you're wearing a gold watch!” Some classmates knew their watches.
Everyone put down their pizza and gathered around Zhao's watch. The other side of the table grew lively; here only Chen Wenwen and Lu Mingfei remained among half-eaten slices.

Lu Mingfei wanted to look too. A good watch was always cool to a boy. Though he knew little about watches, he understood their great significance: like monkeys on South Pacific islands stuffing fruit into their cheeks to create a powerful jawline and attract females. Expensive male adornment. Caesar often wore a Patek Philippe, occasionally switching to a Zenith or Glashütte.
But Lu Mingfei didn't move, because Chen Wenwen hadn't. If he joined the crowd, she would be left alone. She was still texting.

The conversation grew livelier. Several boys wore watches and showed them off, also discussing how so-and-so had bought a Jeep to drive around campus, how another had failed three courses because he took golf lessons, and how another never lived in a dorm but rented a serviced apartment for twelve thousand a month. These subjects were far removed from poor Lu Mingfei. Those people were distant too. The closest person to him now was Chen Wenwen, right before his eyes and as far away as the horizon.
She did not spare him even a glance, texting on and on.

How awkward. Suddenly he missed Fingel. If his useless senior were here, he clearly wouldn't be embarrassed... He'd seize the opportunity to drag the lobster pizza over to himself! Lu Mingfei felt a sudden delight and quietly pulled the whole freshly served lobster pizza close. Smelling the melted cheese, he felt better and laughed without thinking.
The laugh sounded so lewd and sleazy that everyone turned at once. The room suddenly fell quiet.
Lu Mingfei ducked his head.
Chen Wenwen pressed Send.
Zhao Menghua's phone beeped. “You have a new message.”

Lu Mingfei knew whom she was texting. Suddenly it all became clear, a startling discovery: so this was the great advantage of having a girlfriend! Even if you didn't sit together at dinner you could text, talking slowly in a noisy crowd... whether to go out this weekend... whether yesterday's beef-noodle shop was good... a great comic you'd read lately... the flower you'd planted in the botanical garden last year had sprouted... Beep, back and forth.
However noisy the surroundings, the two of you still had a world of your own, quiet enough to hear a flower seed lost in the shade beneath a window last spring begin to sprout.
How literary. Literary enough to make a person sad.

Lu Mingfei's battle-tested eyes were blinded by envy, jealousy, and resentment. Why hadn't he noticed before? Oh, so that was it. He never knew how close other people were in private... He was always an idiot. His thoughts ran wild, and he grinned silently. Sometimes when he didn't know what expression to wear, he smiled like a fool.
Zhao Menghua retrieved his Rolex and put it on. “Eat, everyone, eat.”
Liu Miaomiao sat nearby silently looking at her phone. Everyone else returned to their seats, chewing pizza and cursing some professor for being such a maniac.
The atmosphere was strangely stifling.
“I'm going to the restroom.” Lu Mingfei stood.
At the waiter's “squat toilet,” Lu Mingfei held a wad of paper and assumed the standard squatting position, but he was actually thinking. Suddenly many things tumbled through his mind.

On Nono's birthday, her official boyfriend Caesar had been leading the Student Council's lovely girls in white lace dresses around campus with submachine guns to slay a dragon, while Lu Mingfei and Nono watched the stars by the cold spring on the hill. Nono had placed her phone on a rock, waiting for someone's birthday wishes. He had sat beside her, kicking the icy water, feeling in tune with the red-haired little witch. Later he had given her a sky full of fireworks. His heart had stirred with foolish hopes.

One afternoon he and Chen Wenwen had classroom-cleaning duty. She sat on the teacher's platform with a faint smile, head bowed over her phone. He happily waved his mop and ran around, because in a world the size of the classroom only he and Chen Wenwen existed. He felt incredibly close to her, as if even holding hands wasn't impossible. Foolish hopes stirred.

At the Literature Club graduation gathering, he and Chen Wenwen returned from booking movie tickets and walked beside the river. She texted with her head down, her sleeve brushing his shoulder. A little deer bounded in his heart... No! Hundreds of two-and-a-half-meter stags with huge antlers crashed exuberantly around his chest, making his nose threaten to bleed and his face glow. He felt the moment belonged to him and Chen Wenwen and wished the road could stretch to the edge of the sky... Foolish hopes stirred...
Damn it! Was “foolish hopes stirring” all worth writing in the history of his love life?

Every time his hopes stirred, the other person had been sending or awaiting a text. A young hero and heroine ride one horse across a vast grassland, sky wide, clouds low, a lone goose calling in the west wind; he in white, she in red, and he wishes the moment could last forever. Meanwhile the heroine's lips move as she uses a long-distance voice technique to exchange love songs with her boyfriend far to the south. What kind of crap plot was that? What garbage writer would create such a pathetic male lead?
But if Lu Mingfei lived in a book... the book had been written by a garbage writer... and he was that utterly pathetic male lead.
No, not the lead. Just passerby A, B, C, or D.

Sometimes he thought Nono and Caesar didn't talk much and didn't seem particularly close... and foolish hopes stirred. But they were boyfriend and girlfriend, for heaven's sake. When Nono and Caesar were alone together... did they hold hands? Hug? Kiss? Damn it, Boss Caesar looked every inch a handsome, debauched, sex-starved devil!

The saddest thing in the world was secretly loving a girl while she happily shared her life with someone else. While you walked alone in moonlight, thinking of her in literary sorrow, under that same moon she held someone's hand, leaned into someone's arm, and kissed someone's lips... The air was full of the hormones of mutual desire...

Lu Mingfei picked at a crack in the floor tiles in grief and indignation, convinced no one in the vast world was sadder than he. Then he remembered he was in a restroom, and that crack in the tiles... A wave of nausea abruptly halted the melancholy literary mood in his head.
A text chimed. With the finger that had picked the tile crack held up delicately, Lu Mingfei extracted his phone and opened it.

“Happy birthday, wishing you a happy birthday, happiness every day of your life, never mind how you spend your birthday... I've learned Zheng Zhihua's 'Happy Birthday.' It's the first Chinese song I can sing. The attachment is my recording, your birthday present. As you know, your senior is dirt poor, so let's skip gifts that cost money.” Sender: Useless Senior.
That was his roommate Fingel. Lu Mingfei had given him that name in his contacts as revenge: Fingel listed Lu Mingfei as Idiot Junior.

Lu Mingfei was touched. It was rare for anything in his useless senior's shaggy head to remember his birthday. The emotion didn't last long... because he couldn't resist opening the attachment. Fingel sang in German-accented Mandarin, wildly off-key being a perfect description, but he put force into every word and had clearly made an effort. Only... wasn't this “Happy Birthday” that song by the old-school literary singer from the 1980s?

“Your birthday reminds me of a friend from long ago. It was a cold winter, and he wandered the streets. I thought he wanted to beg for something, but he always shook his head...” Fingel sang on with extravagant feeling.
Was a song this miserable really a birthday greeting? It sounded more like something to play at his grave. Lu Mingfei covered his face and sighed deeply.
He closed the attachment, pulled up his baggy shorts, and stood. Looking up, he saw a line of neat writing on the partition: “I'm very boyish... seeking a lesbian... phone 138XXXXXXXX.”
“Someone looking for a lesbian in the men's room?” He stared.
Wait!
His head buzzed. Something was wrong! Seeking a lesbian in the men's room plainly defied ordinary logic, but with a different way of thinking... everything made sense!
Damn it! Depressed when he came in, he hadn't checked the sign on the door!
Holding up his shorts, half squatting, legs weak, he couldn't stand up. No way. The wrong room again? Once was an accident, twice was natural absentmindedness, three times... that was a hobby!

He rapidly considered countermeasures. There was no time for hesitation. Only a few meters separated the stall from the door; if no one noticed, he could sprint out in three to five seconds. He tried combing his hair forward to hide his face. The look might barely pass for... a tomboy?
He pricked up his ears. It was quiet outside; apparently still safe. Relieved, he fastened his shorts and loosened his ankles as though preparing for a hundred-meter sprint.
“Did you tell her or not?” A girl's voice came from the corridor outside.
“It has nothing to do with her. Why should I?” a boy answered impatiently.
“If you don't tell her she'll find out sooner or later. Can you avoid seeing each other forever?”
“You know what she's like. She's exhausting, moping all day. What good would telling her do? She'd cling to me as though I owed her something.”
“Don't talk about her like that... When you were together, didn't you say she was pretty nice?” The girl's voice grew quieter.

“How was I supposed to know what she was like at first? Oversensitive for no reason, playing gloomy one moment, pitiful the next, then unbearably bossy, as if the world had to revolve around her. Whoever wants to cater to her can do it. I'm done!”
“If we broke up someday... you wouldn't talk about me like that too, would you?”

“Come on, you're different from her. I'd never say that about you. I tell everyone how great you are... Damn, wrong answer. That day will never come. We won't break up! I'd have to hit my head to break up with you.” The boy laughed ingratiatingly.
“Stop it! Why are you all over me?”
“Pretty skirt... Did you buy it in Yunnan?”
The jumbled sounds of kissing, fabric rubbing, footsteps, and soft murmurs faded away. Lu Mingfei turned to stone, his head buzzing.
Zhao Menghua and Liu Miaomiao had just passed along the corridor outside.
“Kissing and groping right there. Did they think I didn't exist?” Lu Mingfei muttered.

Of their three class beauties, Chen Wenwen, Liu Miaomiao, and Su Xiaoqiang, Zhao Menghua had hooked two: when the class flowers bloomed, he was the one smiling among them... A real winner in life. Once Lu Mingfei understood, righteous indignation filled him! Not just for himself, but for all the boys in class. There were already more boys than girls, and Zhao was taking more than his share! What was this? A waste of resources!
He was also a little dazed. The world changed so quickly. It was as though you looked up and everyone had gone far ahead, leaving you, a little kid, standing where you were.
He pushed open the stall door and walked out, then abruptly stopped.

In the mirror above the sinks he saw Sadako: white dress, black hair hanging over her face. Both hands were beneath the faucet, but the water wasn't running. She stood frozen in the posture of washing them.
At that moment he would rather it had really been Sadako, slowly crawling out of the mirror. At worst he could have screamed, “A ghost!”
But it was Chen Wenwen.
“I-I... came into the wrong restroom...” he explained. Only after speaking did he realize how irrelevant that was.

As though she hadn't seen him, Chen Wenwen turned on the faucet, wet her hands, and patted water onto her face. Her phone lay on the sink. When she reached for it, she fumbled; it clattered to the floor and slid across the tiles toward Lu Mingfei.

He slowly bent to pick it up, looked at her expression, and carefully offered it back. His curiosity was too strong. His eyes darted to the messages on the screen. Chen Wenwen used an iPhone too; its messaging system displayed all the texts with one person like a chat log, stringing scattered memories together.
“You're not wearing the bracelet I gave you last birthday...”
“Did you get my text just now? The one about the bracelet...”
“Got it. I'm not wearing it today. Too hot.”
“Yes, it's too hot. I couldn't sleep last night, kept thinking about the past. I could only sleep an hour or two at a time. Did you sleep well?”
“All right. Drink a glass of milk before bed and you'll sleep.”
“Do you still think about me?”
“Don't overthink it. We're still classmates.”

“Last night I dreamed I was rowing down a river. I texted to ask where you were, and you said you were waiting on the bridge ahead. I rowed forward, but there was fog everywhere and I rowed a long time without seeing a bridge. I texted again and you said you were still waiting on the bridge. I wondered if it was behind me and rowed hard back, but the current was too fast, so I kept going forward... Then I woke up.”
“Don't overthink it. Calm your mind and you won't dream.”
“Do you understand what the dream means?”
“Yes, but I don't want to hear it. There's no point. Saying less is better for both of us.”
“You don't want to hear me anymore. Do you have a new girlfriend?”
“Stop asking! We're at a gathering today. Let me eat in peace! You keep texting, and Lu Mingfei beside you can see!”
“Don't be angry. If you've found a new girlfriend, I'll wish...”
That final text was unfinished. Now there was no need to send it.

Want to wish them well? Easy: go out at once, buy flowers, rush in, and give them to Liu Miaomiao, saying, Little sister, you're wonderful; I can rest easy knowing Zhao Menghua is with you... But was that really what she wanted to say? Bless them? Bullshit. Even Lu Mingfei, whose romantic experience was a blank canvas fit for the most beautiful picture, wouldn't fall for it!
His face twitched. He didn't know what expression to wear.

Actually he had reason to smile smugly. The girl you once liked gave you a polite rejection and threw herself into the arms of a glamorous young prince, and now he'd dumped her. If the petty heart inside you didn't laugh a little, who would believe it? Karma never failed! Ha ha ha! Shouldn't you kick her while she was down, saying, “You thought I was a loser, but my feelings were sincere and dependable. What did that playboy have apart from money and looks?” Or you could be more gentlemanly and say considerately, “It'll pass. Who hasn't had their heart broken?” while secretly exulting, That's for kicking me aside!
But Lu Mingfei only scratched his head and sighed.

He was too timid, so timid he scarcely had a vengeful thought. In a dream Lu Mingze had asked, “Don't you want revenge on the world?” Lu Mingfei had never really thought about it. Not only that, he constantly handed out sympathy, even to Chen Wenwen, who had given him the polite rejection.
Reading the messages, he felt that Chen Wenwen was exhausted and had used all her strength. Her face was wet and pale, so tired it hurt to see.
“Don't look,” she said softly, taking the phone from his hand and switching off the screen. “It's all right.”
“Oh, okay.” He nodded quickly.

Chen Wenwen lifted her long white skirt to wipe her face, arranged her hair, took a deep breath, and straightened her chest. A resentful woman? Not at all. She looked more like Joan of Arc going into battle.
“Don't say anything. Promise.” She looked at Lu Mingfei in the mirror.

She had always spoken to him like that. In the Literature Club, when she assigned him something such as arranging the venue, she would say, “Make sure it's arranged. Promise,” as if his promise could really guarantee anything.
“Mm. I promise.” As before, he raised his hand.
They returned to the room, where a fresh round of pizza had arrived. Everyone was cheerful. It seemed the party was livelier without the two of them.

Lu Mingfei ate absently, watching the people around him. They all seemed different now. He noticed details: Zhao Menghua took two slices and tore one off for Liu Miaomiao; she absentmindedly drank his cola; the boys who used to praise her beauty no longer stole glances at the slender legs beneath her skirt; Zhao and Liu sat close together and far from the others.
Suddenly he understood. When it came to feelings he was a complete idiot. He had never understood other people's looks. Everything he thought he knew was wrong.

Zhao Menghua glanced at Chen Wenwen opposite him, a strange light flashing in his eyes. He cleared his throat and reached into his pocket like a leader about to make a speech. Liu Miaomiao hurriedly pulled at him under the table, but he shook her off.
Lu Mingfei suddenly felt uneasy. He didn't know what Zhao intended, but instinct told him it would be idiotic, stupid, and had to be stopped, even if that meant pouring a glass of cola over his head.
Damn it, why was his glass always empty at moments like this?

Zhao stood with a blue velvet jewelry box in hand and looked around the table. “Since everyone's here today, I'll announce something...” He glanced down at Liu Miaomiao, who instinctively avoided his eyes, cheeks flushed as though she had drunk a great deal.
He opened the box. Inside was a Tiffany platinum wire ring. “Nobody's allowed to pursue Liu Miaomiao anymore. Anyone who does answers to me... We're getting engaged. This is the engagement ring.”
Everyone fell silent. Though they knew about Zhao and Liu, engagement... in freshman year? What grand family still played the engagement game?
“Boss, your family actually lets you get engaged?” a follower asked.

“Hell, my mom kept saying if I thought she was right, I should make it official. Mom bought the ring herself. What? Got a problem? I'm telling you so nobody tries to pursue her without knowing and runs into a wall.” Zhao grinned and surveyed the table, his eyes not pausing on Chen Wenwen.
“Of course it's fine! So that's why we're having lunch. If I'd known, I'd have bought a present,” the follower said quickly.
“Zhao Menghua, you're ruthless. Engaged as soon as you win her over, leaving us brothers no hope at all,” someone congratulated him with a mournful face.
“Then we should order a few beers.”
“Bumpkin! For something this big it has to be champagne. You think Zhao Menghua can't afford it? If we don't fleece him now, when will we?”
“Come on, put the ring on her! Pictures! Can we post them in the alumni group?”
“Happy now? I've told everyone.” Zhao grinned at Liu Miaomiao. “Now you're tied to me for good... marry a carrying pole and you have to carry it around...”
“Stop it...” She lowered her head and pinched his waist.
“Ow, look, she's hitting me...” Zhao laughed and teased his girlfriend—no, now his fiancée.
While the room buzzed with celebration, outside everyone's gaze, a person silently crumbled, as though consumed by fire until only ashes remained.
“Hey, man, you...” Someone stood, the corner of his eye twitching, and stared at Zhao Menghua. “Have you no decency?”
The room fell dead silent. Everyone looked at Lu Mingfei as though they had seen Godzilla.

Lu Mingfei understood why Zhao had done it. He had to give his current girlfriend an assurance. Anyone who landed Liu Miaomiao would be so happy he'd parade around campus banging a lunch basin and blowing snot bubbles, wishing everyone knew he had claimed that flower. Zhao had been fairly careful today, holding back because Chen Wenwen didn't know yet. But Liu had a knot in her heart, and Zhao had to make a gesture. By evening news of the engagement would spread across the school; everyone would know what a devoted boyfriend he was, and from then on Zhao and Liu would be bound together openly and properly.

But Lu Mingfei had something to say. He wanted to say... She already knows, she's been struggling to hold herself together and can't much longer, she won't text you anymore or nag you... What are you showing off for with your arm around your new girlfriend? We all know how cool and handsome you are, big brother! Of course you won't lack girlfriends! Your life must be wonderfully happy, with a girlfriend to eat late-night snacks with, unlike a loser like me... Oh, right, nothing to do with me... In short, all those thousands of words came down to one sentence:
“You're already happy... just leave her a way to live!”
Lu Mingfei delivered his bold, powerful speech in his head, but not one word escaped his mouth.
He glanced at Chen Wenwen, who was close to falling apart, and sighed. He knew her personality: if he said those things, she would suffer most.

So he could only puff out his cheeks and glare at Zhao Menghua with eyes that were neither quite timid nor quite arrogant, so much white showing around the irises. In high school his homeroom teacher had once said before the whole class, “Lu Mingfei, are you really that useless? Are you a dead weight? You alone dragged our class average down half a point. You're unbelievable.” Lu had answered with the same stare, impossible to tell whether it was stupidity or defiance, and made the teacher's heart race.
Lu Mingfei was confident that stare was still quite lethal... Apart from that he didn't have much killing power.

Actually, playing the brave young defender was not for him; this was the situation he handled worst. He instinctively feared awkward scenes. Watching Tom Hanks in Cast Away, for example, Hanks lived like a savage on an island for years after a plane crash, yearning to return to his wife and child. After endless hardship he finally got home, emotions surging at the door—Hanks didn't yet know his wife had remarried, but Lu Mingfei watching did. So he would urgently change channels to avoid embarrassment that had nothing to do with him. He couldn't bear the door opening and Hanks seeing his wife approach in tears on a strange man's arm. Even a movie scene was unbearable.
But this time his brain had overheated and he had run right into the scene himself, playing a passerby with a sense of justice. Really, what the hell did any of it have to do with him?
Zhao Menghua's face twisted, his brow knotted as though the god Erlang's third eye lay hidden there, ready to open and stare the damned monkey before him to death.
“None of your damn business!” He spat the words like a deadly dart from an outlaw's mouth.
“You're right,” Lu Mingfei said.
Zhao froze. He had prepared several more concise and vicious replies for when Lu finished talking tough. But Lu Mingfei had readily admitted it.
Yet Lu didn't move away, still holding that wide-eyed stare.
“What do you want?” Zhao stepped forward.
“Nothing.” It was true. Lu hadn't had time to think. Given a minute to consider, he might well have retreated.
Zhao nearly broke down, veins jumping in his neck, but several friends held him back. “We're classmates... Forget it, forget it.”

Zhao took a deep breath, glared at Lu, and forced out through his teeth, “Pay the bill! We're leaving! What are we eating for? I've lost my appetite! I'll take you all somewhere else for Italian tonight!”

Lu Mingfei breathed easier. Good. Let it end here, leaving room to retreat. Hybrids were supposed to have exceptional physical abilities; Caesar's beautiful Student Council combat squad could take on 200-pound wrestlers in high heels and evening gowns. But that advantage had never appeared in Lu Mingfei, and he had yet to take a fighting class. If it came to blows, two of him would be no match for Zhao. He glanced at Chen Wenwen. She stared blankly into a corner, as though the scene had nothing to do with her.
“The emperor isn't worried, but the eunuch is...” Lu Mingfei muttered inwardly.

The bill came. Zhao pulled several notes from his wallet and tossed them onto the tray, then thought better of it, took one back, and pointed at Lu. “This one pays for himself! Nothing to do with me!”
“Fine, I'll pay for myself.” Lu wasn't afraid of that; instead, his spirits rose.

A Cassell student ID was also an American Express credit card with a hundred-thousand-dollar limit! Though he was penniless, he could borrow from an American bank by swiping it! Without thinking he took out his student card. Nicknamed the black card, it had a matte-black surface stamped in pure silver with the college emblem, the half-rotten World Tree. With the gesture of an emperor handing out a tip, he held it between two fingers and passed it to the server.
“We don't take library cards...” The young waitress spoke timidly.
Dark lines covered Lu Mingfei's face. “Get the card machine... I'll show you...”

Someone drew a sharp breath. The back of the card bore both the Citi Bank and American Express logos. Shilan students considered themselves worldly and knew what an American Express black card meant. The highest black card had no spending limit and was called the Centurion; only a very small number of credit cards were permitted to be pure black.
The waitress quickly brought the terminal. Lu entered his PIN with an air of surveying all beneath him, spinning the pen in his palm as he waited for the slip to sign.
“Fake. Declined,” the waitress said in her local accent, the words sounding like “tragedy.”
It really was a tragedy. The terminal displayed PAYMENT DECLINED.

Sweating coldly, Lu swiped the black card he carried everywhere, the symbol of his incomparable S-rank status, again and again. It was refused each time, as though the mighty organization in North America had abandoned him.
Someone laughed, and sneers rose around the room.
“Pay cash,” someone said mildly.

The door opened and air stirred, like breaking the clay seal on a jar to let in a cool breeze. The young man entering placed several large notes in the black billfold and returned it to the waitress. “Keep the change.”

Only a class enemy could utter such punchable words; normally anyone hearing them ought to give him the finger. But this boy spoke with natural detachment, without a trace of showiness. No one noticed how he had suddenly entered, without a sound. He wore faded jeans and a white T-shirt, enormous sunglasses, and no expression on the half of his face visible.
Such a figure looked ordinary enough to be found on any street, nothing remarkable. But Liu Miaomiao suddenly stood, staring at him, tense.

Lu Mingfei also sprang up, tense. But his tension was different from hers. His instinct was that something had happened; why else would these human-dragon hybrids come looking for him during summer break? And he knew exactly why this fellow carried a tennis bag. Whenever he appeared with any long object, you had to be careful: repeated experience showed he would inevitably draw a blade from it.
“How much longer until lunch ends? The college has something for us to do. I'm here to assist you,” the boy told Lu. “Waiting for you to start, boss.”

Boss? This fellow called him boss? Lu thought he was hearing things. Don't joke! Since when was he this man's boss? Boss Caesar had wanted to take over the Lionheart Society for years, only to be repelled head-on by this harmless-looking fellow.
Yet it didn't seem to be a joke. This man supposedly had no sense of humor whatsoever.
“Chu Zihang. We're all alumni.” The boy briefly removed his sunglasses, then put them back on.
This time everyone turned to stone.
For Shilan students three years above or below him, “Chu Zihang” was a symbol, always far out of reach.
You knew his name and had seen him, but couldn't quite remember his face, because you rarely had a chance to get close.

At graduation he spoke for the student body in a sea-blue uniform, head lowered over his notes and bangs hiding his face. On the basketball court he played center, devastating opponents and leaping to dunk; by the time the ball landed he was already turning back toward midcourt, not even high-fiving teammates. At the Spring Festival show he played a cello solo of the theme from Schindler's List. While the audience remained immersed in the music, thinking his talent belonged on the national gala, Chu Zihang had already packed his cello, bowed, and left the stage, leaving only a slender back.
In Liu Miaomiao's memory, every time she saw Chu Zihang it was raining.

Beyond the eaves rain fell in curtains, mist drifting between the strands. Chu Zihang stood under the roof in a brown denim overshirt, a scarf tied at the collar, hands in his pockets. A bag hung from one shoulder, bulging with what was obviously a basketball. He bent slightly like bamboo in the wind, its joints firm. Faint daylight haloed his dark silhouette.

Liu Miaomiao walked forward surrounded by girls from her class. It felt as though hundreds of little frogs had been stuffed into her heart, jumping furiously. She talked and laughed with the girls as they approached that figure. Each step closer seemed long, so long that time nearly stopped. At last she stood behind him. Chu Zihang politely shifted aside and nodded. She noticed his bangs were wet from the rain, hanging over his eyes.
Time resumed its normal pace. Chu Zihang and Liu Miaomiao passed each other.

After walking a long way, she suddenly turned her head and asked, “Can you see if I have a pimple?” Her classmates leaned close and said no. She said good, it had felt itchy, and quietly withdrew her backward glance.

Through layers of rain Chu Zihang still stood there. Liu Miaomiao had always thought he liked rainy days. Whenever it rained, he seemed so absorbed that she wanted to brush his soaked bangs aside and see his eyes.
Chu Zihang had used his life to define one word: awesome.

So awesome that even a meteoric force like Lu Mingfei could only prostrate himself beneath Brother Chu's slim-fit jeans. The true hidden number one on the “This Villain Must Be Eliminated” list would always be Chu Zihang.

For Liu Miaomiao and many girls at Shilan, Chu Zihang taught them the meaning of an unrequited crush. But he seemed unaware of his mastery in this field, and people misunderstood him. His face was simply expressionless, yet many thought he was pretending to be cool. He didn't like rainy days at all; he stared into space when it rained because he wondered whether that Maybach might come to pick him up again...
Chu Zihang attracted countless admirers but was dense to an extraordinary degree. He was like one of the Easter Island stone statues gazing out to sea; blossoms falling on him were utterly wasted.

Why must he be eliminated? If the many Shilan boys dating girls in their class discovered the same man's shadow had already invaded their girlfriends' hearts, it would be strange if they didn't want to destroy him!
“Thanks, thanks. You're a real friend, senior.” Whatever the circumstances, Lu Mingfei was grateful for Chu Zihang's sudden appearance. “I'll pay you back when we get home.”
“It's nothing. You're the boss today; you make the calls,” Chu Zihang said calmly.

Lu stared. The act was getting more convincing. Who was he to deserve this? It would be an honor to polish the president's shoes, and he dared call himself boss in public? But Chu looked as if to say this was a fact not worth discussing, so he could only keep quiet.

The crowd murmured in amazement. They had known Boss Lu was astonishing, but not that he was so modest, displaying only two parts of his twelve-part greatness. Even Chu Zihang called him boss; surely he had built a vast empire in his year in America. How gracious of him to condescend to eat pizza with his old classmates. That also explained his lack of cash: underlings always paid, so why would the boss settle the bill himself?
“The car's waiting outside.” Chu held the door and gestured for him to go first.

Chu's icy expression made Lu uncertain what was happening. The courtesy lay somewhere between a bodyguard addressing his boss and the CIA addressing a terrorist with nowhere left to run. He realized refusal wasn't an option and walked out with his head down.
Chu followed without missing a step, their footsteps echoing down the hall. Lu thought of the people watching him from behind, eyes full of envy and resentment, but he didn't feel honored at all.

Damn, what rotten luck. It wasn't his business, so why had he stepped in? And once he did, even his credit card had proved as useless as he was. The president had rescued him, but what did that amount to? Every scrap of face Lu Mingfei had ever enjoyed had been provided by his seniors. Not once had he stood up and been impressive on his own. He was like a little kid beaten up in a fight, face covered in snot, who went home to fetch his big brother. Others feared you a little, but never respected you, because even with a fierce, stone-faced fighting brother and a gorgeous, long-legged sister, you were still a little kid with snot on your face.
You are incapable. You are useless.
Chu Zihang opened the Panamera's door. Pure white leather racing seats welcomed the honored guest.
Suddenly Lu Mingfei stopped, turned, and ran back!
The people talking at the door to the private room backed away in alarm and made a path. Lu had returned at a hundred-meter sprint, bristling with murderous intent.
He walked up to Chen Wenwen and reached out... seized the toilet seat leaning against his chair... and dashed out of the door.
Chen Wenwen said nothing, gently brushing her long bangs aside.

“Headquarters has assigned a mission. You're the agent and I'm assisting, so you're the boss today. It's not a joke.” Chu handed Lu an iPad and skillfully steered one-handed as the Panamera joined the stream of traffic.

Lu Mingfei could hardly believe his ears. A mission with him in charge? What task could he excel at enough to have Chu Zihang assist him? Unless they were going as a team to challenge the Deyun Society at comic dialogue, with Lu as the funny man and Chu as his straight man...

But the iPad ran a Cassell-developed interface directly connected to Norma, and his name was plainly listed under AGENT. After reading the details, Lu Mingfei felt lost in a fog. Was this a criminal investigation? But Field Investigation seemed to be a junior-year elective. He was a complete novice in that area... apart from watching Detective Conan movies.
The air conditioning raised goosebumps on his skin. He glanced timidly at Chu Zihang; the hard profile was expressionless and showed no intention of explaining to the person in charge what to do.

His courage failed. He sank into the seat and stared blankly out the window. He was in a bad mood. When Chen Wenwen had brushed back her hair, he had seen her dreadful face. Ugly—she had never looked so ugly, tears clinging to pale skin, eyes swollen... like a little goldfish. Where was the girl of his dreams? Once she had sat at one end of a bench in a white cotton dress reading Duras's The Lover, her spotless fairy aura seeming to banish sunlight and dust alike. Every fairy, apparently, would one day fall for an idiot and knit him sweaters, loving and resentful, and from then on her life was a downhill road of no return. At such a time a toad like Lu Mingfei, who had never tasted swan flesh, ought to clap in delight, but for some reason his heart clenched and he suddenly grew irritable.
“I listened outside the room for two minutes.”
Lu Mingfei nearly jumped out of his skin. Chu had spoken without warning. The flat statement sounded like a threat: I know what you did last summer.

Would the president take an interest in his useless junior's petty gossip and silently listen for two minutes? For a man with Chu Zihang's rigorously organized schedule, what could possibly be important enough to stop him for two minutes?

“You should inform your card issuer of your travel plans. Otherwise, if they see the card used in another place, they'll suspect theft and temporarily freeze the account,” Chu said. “I know you liked Chen Wenwen at school.”
Lu Mingfei's heart lost its rhythm and his face flushed purple. Even when Fingel exposed his feelings for Nono, he hadn't reacted so strongly.

Nono's beauty was dazzling and sharp, an angel bearing a sword, sometimes madly loyal to her friends. Any man ought to like Nono; Lu suspected Fingel liked her too. He had never imagined Nono dumping Caesar and falling into his arms... All right, given their relative strength, Nono would take him into hers. It was pure admiration: a lovely lady, a worthy gentleman's desire, and a loser's desire too. Nothing to be ashamed of, as long as Boss Caesar didn't know.

But Chen Wenwen was different. Chen Wenwen was a secret. When he had been innocent and still capable of embarrassment, he had thought marrying her would be the happiness of his life. He never tired of sitting beside her on a bench reading all afternoon, running Literature Club errands at her heels like an eager little dog. Back then he had never liked anyone else, wasn't thick-skinned, and had experienced nothing momentous. He was an uncool boy weaving a future with this girl in his heart. If she had nodded, he would have impatiently placed his whole life in her hands for her to command... But she hadn't chosen him.

He always wanted to find a hollow tree and bury that story in it, because it was embarrassing, or... because the feeling of loving someone like that was so tender that if people knew, they might touch it and break it.
“You... you...”
“Probably the whole school knew,” Chu added.

“Senior, don't make it sound so scary. The whole school? Our high school banned dating!” Lu felt as if struck by five thunderbolts. “If everyone really knew, wouldn't the dean have dragged me off to confess my wrongdoing?”
“He didn't because he knew you had no chance. He didn't need to concern himself with your fantasies.”
“But surely not the whole school?”
“Someone else liked Chen Wenwen and told people you liked her as a joke. So the whole school knew.”
Lu stared. “Zhao Menghua?”
Chu did not answer.

Lu sat stunned for a long time, suddenly very tired. Nono had said everyone had played him at the Literature Club farewell. But he hadn't wanted to believe it. He thought he had hidden his feelings well; a few people making fun of him wouldn't matter as long as Chen Wenwen wasn't one of them. He would rather she had never known he liked her and therefore chosen Zhao. But if even Chu Zihang could recount his romantic history in detail...
He was that i, lowercase, a very small “I”... but with no love and no you.
“I don't mind you standing on the seat, but at this speed it's unsafe,” Chu said.

Only then did Lu realize he had somehow crouched on the luxurious leather seat, arms around his knees, chin resting on them—a posture somewhere between an elderly northern Shaanxi farmer on a field ridge and a stray dog taking a rest. He hurriedly jumped down, wiped at his shoeprints, and smiled awkwardly.
“It's all right. You weren't saying anything, so I was finding a topic to talk about,” Chu said coldly.

Lu was dumbfounded. Huh? What did that mean? Was this merely the president's icebreaker, like the table-tennis diplomacy that opened relations between China and America? He hadn't had time to wonder why Chu had turned to Chen Wenwen instead of discussing the mission. Was this heart-souring subject merely the stone-faced senior's friendly small talk to break the silence between them? Damn! Table tennis would have been better!
“I'm not Conan...” Lu tried to discuss business.
“Chen Wenwen knew you liked her but pretended she didn't. She wasn't good to you and treated you as a follower. Yet you still stood up for her?” Chu cut off his topic like a blade.
Lu was unaccustomed to such forceful questioning and froze.
“Because she's vulnerable now and you pity her?” Chu shot him a cold glance.
“She was never bad to me. I liked her; that had nothing to do with her.” Lu grew anxious.

“Zhao Menghua was unhappy because Chen Wenwen was his girlfriend. She still loves him, and psychologically he still feels possessive toward her. He can discard her, but he doesn't want anyone else standing up for her.” Chu raised an eyebrow. “Why did you?”

The cold, pressing tone was like a knife digging into his heart. Lu suddenly grew angry. He didn't want to discuss this, but Chu insisted. What did Chu Zihang want? He was only a senior, only president of the Lionheart Society. Lu Mingfei was an underling of Student Council President Caesar, with no connection to the society. Why must he report his romantic history to its president? They were only doing a mission together; afterward they would go their separate ways! What was Chu trying to ask? Did he only want Lu to admit he was an idiot? That girl had set him up and embarrassed him publicly, yet now he insisted on standing up for her?

“All right, I know what you're going to say. I'm an idiot. I'm useless and still try to play the hero, but I... I can't stand seeing someone treated unfairly.” Lu turned hard toward the window, raising his voice. “Anyway, senior, you'd never be treated unfairly! You've been outstanding all your life. You don't understand!”
The Panamera braked suddenly, tires screeching against the road, and stopped dead in the middle of the street.
“Get out,” Chu said.

“What?” Lu was bewildered. The sudden stop had almost given him a concussion. What had he said wrong to be thrown out? Could it be... the president had secretly loved Chen Wenwen for years too, and hearing his rival pour out his heart had made him sulk?
“Get out and wait for me. I have something to do. I'll be right back.” Chu was expressionless.

Sitting in someone else's luxury sports car, arguing was pointless. Lu obediently got out and stood by the road. Chu shifted into reverse and floored the accelerator. The Panamera accelerated backward into traffic with smoke rising from all four wheels, retracing their route.
Lu stared. He had never seen anyone drive so outrageously. He didn't know this was a driving style inherited in certain families.
Sunlight stung the skin, hot air rising in wisps from the asphalt. Chen Wenwen trailed far behind the group. Through the heat the boy's back ahead of her looked distorted.
Everything was distorted.
“Hey, sister-in-law, do you eat foie gras?” someone called.
“No, it's too salty. I'll have a salad. You eat what you like,” Liu Miaomiao answered absently.
“Boss, it's burning up. Why are we wandering outside? Let's get ice cream at Cold Stone,” another said.
“Save room for dinner.” Zhao Menghua's voice came faintly.
The conversation was distant, yet seemed close to her ear.
Sometimes people couldn't help listening closely to words that pierced the heart. Perhaps their brains had short-circuited...
Chen Wenwen looked down at her white sandals. Again and again, her slender fair feet emerged beneath her skirt as she shuffled forward.

When she was still with Zhao, he had come to school to see her and they had walked under the lights after dinner. She had walked with her head down then too. Students passed on their way back from evening study, and whenever someone called, “Chen Wenwen, is this your boyfriend?” her face burned, as if it were embarrassing, yet she felt so happy. Zhao would throw an arm firmly around her shoulders and grin as he greeted them.
Now she still couldn't lift her head. Not from embarrassment, but because it felt so heavy it might break her neck.
Zhao Menghua was annoyed. Since leaving Sophie Lad Pizza, Chen Wenwen had followed them, inexplicably refusing to leave.

What was the point of clinging now? It was over, and she was acting like a resentful wife. Zhao didn't think he had wronged her. It was just a breakup, wasn't it? Before splitting up they had had a terrible fight. Zhao had gritted his teeth and said they should break up, and Chen Wenwen had actually bitten her lip and agreed. Startled, he had said, “If you dare agree, don't regret it!” and stormed out. A few days later he happened to sit beside Liu Miaomiao at a gathering and suddenly felt glad he had broken up. He muted his phone throughout because Chen Wenwen kept texting him, dozens of messages in a day.
He wanted to turn and tell her, Aren't you annoying? I told you not to regret it if you dared agree! Playing the tragic victim afterward is pointless.

But Liu Miaomiao was beside him. Being too harsh to an ex would make his new girlfriend think him ungallant, so Zhao endured it. He liked Liu: she was pretty, agreeable, and from a good family; unlike Chen Wenwen, she didn't argue with him and made him look good before his friends. Conveniently, their fathers were golfing partners. On hearing that her son had a new girlfriend, his mother had clapped delightedly and said, “Good breakup! You and Chen Wenwen weren't suited!”

Zhao agreed. Watching Chen from afar, he had always seen her reading quietly, untouched by dust, eyes lowered, utterly lovely. Only after winning her had he learned the more literary they were, the more annoying, oversensitive about everything.
Chen Wenwen also thought she and Zhao Menghua weren't suited.

They had not seen each other for nearly two months. He didn't answer her calls, and emails sank without a trace. Late at night she stared at his QQ status. One weekend he'd gone rafting, the next to an amusement park, the next hiking on Fragrant Hill... Every weekend he had something to do. With whom? She didn't know.

She sat by the library's floor-to-ceiling window. Outside the light was dim and wind stirred the dense green leaves. She remembered The Lover and Marguerite Duras, imagining the girl on the Mekong River slowly turning gray.
Suddenly she burst into sobs, frightening the elderly librarian so badly his chronic leg pain flared up.
Actually the story of The Lover was nothing like hers.
The only thing they shared was being unsuited. The white girl and wealthy Chinese young master in The Lover had parted forever because they were unsuited too.

She had come today to see Zhao. That hope had overcome her heavy hesitation. She had put on light makeup so she would look healthier and he wouldn't worry. She had invited Lu Mingfei because everyone else at the gathering was one of Zhao's friends, which frightened her a little. She hadn't imagined getting back together with Zhao; she only wanted to see him casually.
Then why had she burst into tears?
Why was she still following them?

She knew doing so wouldn't make Zhao look back. She knew his character better than anyone... But if she left like this, perhaps she would never see him again, and all those memories would be gone. In memory they walked side by side beneath streetlights along the school river road; now the lights had gone out. In memory they got meals together in the cafeteria; now the food had spoiled. In memory she had bought a Hello Kitty charm and insisted on hanging it on Zhao's phone. By now, she thought, it must have been torn off. The little pink furry cat lay in a garbage heap somewhere in the world beneath all kinds of filth, but it couldn't even cry, because it had no mouth...
She regretted it. She should never have bought that Hello Kitty. If she hadn't, the kitten would still be lying obediently in the display case waiting for someone to take it home.
Why make that innocent little cat so miserable because of a relationship that wasn't right?
That poor... little cat...
At last tears spilled from her eyes, falling onto the scorching concrete tiles and rising as a faint wisp of steam.
“Hey! Hey!” Xu Yanyan nudged Zhao in the waist with his elbow. Out of the corner of his eye he had seen Chen Wenwen stop, tears streaming, and felt a little pity.
“Will you stop bothering me?” Zhao forcefully knocked his arm away.

He wished he could strike Chen Wenwen instead. She was too annoying! He couldn't bear it. What did she want? If she hadn't come today and they met alone another time, he would have patted her shoulder and comforted her. But she insisted on coming; if she came, she shouldn't cause trouble, and she'd even brought Lu Mingfei. That boy was really stubbornly devoted to her. Now she had made everyone part on bad terms. What more did she want? His new girlfriend Liu Miaomiao was beside him, and he had to take his friends out for Italian that night to recover his standing. He hadn't invited Chen Wenwen. Who did she think she was, following along?

Suddenly a deep, powerful engine sounded. Before Zhao could look up, hot wind cut past as though it might slice his hair. A dark-blue shape flashed beside him; brakes screamed, and the Panamera stopped sharply beside Chen Wenwen.
The lunatic was driving backward!

The window lowered. Chu Zihang's face, half hidden by dark glasses, was icy enough to play a killer utterly loyal to his boss in any Hong Kong film. He said, “Lu Mingfei says he'd like to take you to dinner tonight.”
“Yes, you.” He nodded to the bewildered Chen Wenwen. His handsome, thoroughly masculine face seemed to say, It's that simple. I've delivered the boss's message.

His seriousness, commanding presence, coldness, and nosiness combined perfectly. This was probably an invitation no one could refuse. Imagine someone admired you and invited you to an intimate, elegant dinner for two, but delivered the invitation so forcefully that you felt if you said no, the messenger would pull a Desert Eagle from the glove compartment and shoot you between the eyes...
“He reserved a table at Aspasia tonight.” Chu drew a business card from the compartment and handed it to Chen. “The address is on here. Seven thirty.”

She stared at the black card. Aspasia. She had vaguely heard of this fashionable Italian restaurant, luxurious to an almost unimaginable degree. Could this really be the timid boy's doing? Such unmistakable commanding presence... Boss Lu stood tall and firm!

Nearby the Shilan boys stared, jaws nearly hitting the ground. Given the temperature of the pavement, one might soon smell roasted jaws. Zhao clenched his fists. He had a premonition that an opponent he had never respected was about to crush him again...
“Are you refusing?” Chu frowned.
Could anyone refuse that tone? He was plainly growing impatient. Surely his Desert Eagle was itching to come out of the glove compartment. Even Zhao felt refusing would be courting death.
Chen lowered her head, smoothed the fine hair by her ear, and sniffed. “All right.”
The window rose and the Panamera sped away, arriving and departing in a rush. Its four exhaust pipes again left Zhao's ears ringing.
